t.1.22.1: When the night had given way to dawn, the great sage Viśvāmitra spoke to Kākutstha, who lay upon a bed of leaves.
t.1.22.3: Having heard the most noble words of that sage, the two heroic sons of the king bathed, offered water libations, and recited the supreme prayer in silent repetition.
t.1.22.2: O Rāma, Kausalyā is blessed in her noble son; the morning twilight is dawning. Arise, O tiger among men, for the daily rites owed to the gods must be performed.
t.1.22.4: Having performed their daily rites, the two heroes of great valor, filled with joy, saluted Viśvāmitra, whose wealth was his austerity, and stood before him ready to set out.
t.1.22.5: The two of great valour set forth, and then, there at the auspicious confluence of the Sarayū, they beheld the divine river Tripathagā.
t.1.22.6: There lies the holy hermitage of the sages of fierce splendour, who for many thousands of years have been practising the supreme austerity.
t.1.22.7: Seeing that holy hermitage, the two Rāghavas, filled with the greatest delight, spoke these words to the great-souled Viśvāmitra.
t.1.22.8: Whose is this holy hermitage, and what man dwells in it? O blessed one, we two wish to hear, for great indeed is our curiosity.
t.1.22.9: Hearing those words of the two, the foremost of sages laughed and said: “Listen, Rāma, to whom this hermitage belonged in former times.”
t.1.22.10: Kandarpa was once embodied, he who is called Kāma by the wise.
t.1.22.11: Here the foolish one assailed Sthāṇu, the lord of the gods, who was practicing austerities, collected through self-discipline, and who, having married, was going about with the host of Maruts; and he was roared at with a menacing 'huṃ' by the great-souled one.
t.1.22.12: O Raghunandana, as that evil-minded one was burned by the fierce eye of Rudra, all the limbs of his own body crumbled and fell away from it.
t.1.22.13: There, the body of him who was burnt up by the great-souled one was destroyed; Kāma was made bodiless by the lord of the gods in his wrath.
t.1.22.14: From that time on, O Rāghava, he has been renowned as Anaṅga, and that glorious realm where he cast off his body is the land of Aṅga.
t.1.22.16: O Rāma of auspicious appearance, let us spend the night here today between these two holy rivers; tomorrow we shall cross over.
t.1.22.15: This holy hermitage is his, and these sages were once his disciples, devoted to dharma, O hero; no sin is found in them.
t.1.22.18: Having first offered water for the hands, water for the feet, and hospitality to the son of Kuśika, they afterwards performed the rites of hospitality for Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa.
t.1.22.17: While they were conversing there, the sages, discerning their ascetic power with far-seeing vision, were supremely pleased and were filled with joy.
t.1.22.19: Having received hospitality, they then dwelt there very happily at the hermitage of Kāma, while he delighted them with stories.
